intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer, flying from NYC

experiences.name: Sunrise Swim at Elafonissi Beach
experiences.description: Visit the famous pink-sand Elafonissi Beach in Crete at sunrise to enjoy the shallow turquoise lagoons and stunning colors before the midday heat sets in. The unique pink hue comes from crushed shells and coral. Spend the morning snorkeling and wading through the shallow waters. Retreat to a nearby taverna for shade and refreshments by late morning.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) in the cooler morning hours. Sample local cheeses, olives, cured meats, fresh seafood, and traditional Greek pastries like spanakopita and bougatsa. Chat with local vendors and learn about Greek culinary traditions. This indoor-friendly market is a perfect alternative on hot or rainy days, offering an authentic taste of everyday Greek life.

experiences.name: Evening Meze Dinner in Thessaloniki's Ladadika District
experiences.description: As the sun sets and temperatures cool, head to the vibrant Ladadika neighborhood for a traditional Greek meze dinner. Order a spread of grilled octopus, saganaki (fried cheese), tzatziki, dolmades, and fresh bread paired with local ouzo or tsipouro. Thessaloniki is considered Greece's food capital, and this lively district offers dozens of authentic tavernas with outdoor seating perfect for a breezy evening meal.

experiences.name: Sunset Catamaran Cruise around Santorini Caldera
experiences.description: Board a small-group catamaran in the late afternoon to sail around the volcanic Santorini caldera. Swim in the warm Aegean Sea at volcanic hot springs, snorkel over lava formations, and watch the world-famous Santorini sunset from the water. A light Greek dinner with wine is typically included on board. The evening timing avoids the intense midday heat while offering the most spectacular lighting for photos.

experiences.name: Indoor Greek Cooking Class in Heraklion
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class held in a traditional Cretan kitchen, ideal for avoiding midday heat or rainy weather. Learn to prepare authentic Cretan dishes such as dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and loukoumades (honey doughnuts). The instructor sources ingredients from local markets and explains the history and health benefits of the Mediterranean diet. You'll enjoy eating everything you cook as a full meal at the end.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 into central Athens — both budget-friendly options under €10. Check into your budget hostel or guesthouse in the Monastiraki or Psiri neighborhood. Freshen up and get oriented.
day_by_day.evening: Take a relaxed evening stroll through Monastiraki Square and the Plaka neighborhood. Admire the illuminated Acropolis from street level. Browse the lively flea market streets and soak in the atmosphere of your first night in Greece.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick gyros wrap from a street kiosk near the airport or on arrival in Athens (€2–3)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local taverna in Psiri — try souvlaki plate with pita, tzatziki, and a Greek salad for €8–10. Look for places with handwritten menus and locals dining inside.

day_by_day.notes: Use the Metro Line 3 from the airport to Monastiraki station for about €9 — it's the most straightforward budget option. Validate your ticket before boarding. Athens tap water is safe to drink, saving money on bottled water.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Acropolis early (opens at 8:00 AM) to beat the heat and crowds. Explore the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and Propylaea. The combined ticket (€20–30 depending on season) also covers several other archaeological sites in Athens — great value. Bring water and sunscreen.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down to the Ancient Agora of Athens (included in the combined ticket). Explore the well-preserved Temple of Hephaestus and the Stoa of Attalos museum. Afterward, wander through the Monastiraki flea market for cheap souvenirs and people-watching.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Thissio neighborhood for sunset views of the Acropolis from the pedestrian promenade. Enjoy the golden hour light on the ancient ruins from below — completely free and stunning.

meals.breakfast: Bougatsa (custard-filled pastry) and a Greek coffee at a local bakery near your hostel — €2–3
meals.lunch: Spanakopita (spinach pie) or tiropita (cheese pie) from a street bakery near Monastiraki — €1.50–2.50
meals.dinner: Taverna dinner in Thissio or Psiri — grilled octopus, horiatiki salad, and house wine. Budget €10–13 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Acropolis can be very hot by midday in June — start as early as possible. Wear comfortable walking shoes as the marble paths can be slippery. The combined archaeological ticket is valid for 5 days.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Archaeological Museum (one of the world's great museums) — entry is around €10. Spend 2–3 hours exploring ancient Greek artifacts, the Antikythera Mechanism, and stunning bronze statues. Located in the Exarchia neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Exarchia neighborhood — Athens' bohemian quarter with street art, independent bookshops, and a vibrant local scene. Visit Strefi Hill for a free panoramic view of Athens. Then head to the Central Market (Varvakios Agora) to see local vendors selling fresh fish, meat, olives, and spices.
day_by_day.evening: Take the tram or bus to the coastal suburb of Glyfada for a sunset walk along the waterfront promenade. Enjoy the sea breeze and watch locals enjoy their evening volta (stroll).

meals.breakfast: Koulouri (sesame bread ring) from a street vendor — €0.50, plus Greek yogurt with honey from a nearby café — €2
meals.lunch: Eat at the Central Market area — fresh ingredients or a cheap taverna lunch (mageirefta — daily cooked dishes) for €5–7
meals.dinner: Fresh seafood at a simple psarotaverna (fish tavern) in Glyfada — grilled sardines or calamari with bread and salad for €10–12

day_by_day.notes: The Central Market is closed on Sundays. Exarchia has a lively political atmosphere — perfectly safe for tourists but worth knowing. Tram to Glyfada runs from Syntagma and costs about €1.40.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning bus or ferry from Piraeus port to the island of Aegina (about 1 hour, €8–10 round trip by ferry). Arrive and rent a bicycle or take a local bus to the Temple of Aphaia — a remarkably preserved ancient temple with sea views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Aegina Town beach or the quieter Agia Marina beach on the other side of the island. Swim in the clear Saronic Gulf waters, relax on the sand, and enjoy your first proper Greek beach experience. June temperatures are perfect — warm but not scorching.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Piraeus by ferry in the late afternoon/early evening. Head back to Athens and enjoy a quiet evening in the Plaka neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure or grab something at Piraeus port — a cheese pie or pastry for €1.50
meals.lunch: Fresh fish lunch at a harbourside taverna in Aegina Town — the island is famous for its pistachios, so grab a bag too! Lunch €8–10
meals.dinner: Simple dinner back in Athens — a mezze spread of hummus, taramasalata, olives, and pita at a mezedopoleio for €8–10

day_by_day.notes: Aegina is one of the most accessible and affordable day-trip islands from Athens. Buy ferry tickets at the port — no need to book far in advance for this route. Bring a towel and sunscreen for the beach.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take the KTEL bus from Athens (Kifissos Bus Terminal) to Nafplio in the Peloponnese — about 2.5 hours, €13–15. Nafplio is one of Greece's most charming towns and a perfect budget base. Check into a budget guesthouse in the old town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Nafplio's beautiful Venetian old town on foot — completely free. Walk the narrow cobblestone streets, admire the colorful neoclassical buildings, and visit the Syntagma Square. Climb up to the Acronafplia fortress for free panoramic views over the Argolic Gulf.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the waterfront promenade at sunset. Watch the fishing boats come in and enjoy the relaxed pace of this small coastal town.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Athens hostel if included, or a quick pastry before the bus
meals.lunch: Grab a gyros or souvlaki wrap in Nafplio old town upon arrival — €2.50–3
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local taverna in Nafplio — fresh catch of the day, Greek salad, and local wine for €10–12. Ask locals for their favorite spot.

day_by_day.notes: The KTEL bus departs from Kifissos Terminal A in Athens — take a taxi or bus to get there. Nafplio is very walkable and most attractions are free or very cheap. The town gets busy on weekends with Athenian visitors.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the ancient theater of Epidaurus (about 30 km from Nafplio — take a local KTEL bus for €3–4 each way). The acoustics of this 4th-century BC theater are legendary. Also explore the Sanctuary of Asclepius archaeological site. Combined entry around €12.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Nafplio and spend the afternoon at Arvanitia Beach — a small but lovely pebble beach just a 10-minute walk from the old town. Swim in the crystal-clear water and relax. Alternatively, take the small boat taxi (€5 return) to Bourtzi Castle on the tiny island in the harbor.
day_by_day.evening: Climb the 999 steps up to Palamidi Fortress (entry €8) for spectacular sunset views over Nafplio and the gulf. The climb takes about 20–25 minutes but the views are absolutely worth it.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with local honey and walnuts at a café in Nafplio — €3–4
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snack at Epidaurus — bring food from town to save money, or eat at the site café
meals.dinner: Fresh grilled fish at a waterfront taverna in Nafplio — ask for the daily catch. Budget €11–13 with a carafe of local wine.

day_by_day.notes: The summer solstice! June 21 is the longest day of the year — perfect for the Palamidi sunset climb. Epidaurus also hosts a famous summer festival of ancient Greek drama — check if any performances coincide with your visit (tickets from €15).

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take the KTEL bus from Nafplio toward Corinth and then connect to Patras, or take a direct bus toward the ferry port of Igoumenitsa or Patras. Today you head to the island of Corfu via ferry from Igoumenitsa (about 1.5 hours, €10–15). Alternatively, take a bus to Patras and ferry to Corfu (longer but scenic).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Corfu Town (Kerkyra). Check into a budget hostel or guesthouse. Explore the UNESCO-listed Corfu Old Town — a stunning blend of Venetian, French, and British architecture. Walk through the narrow kantounia (alleyways) and visit the Liston promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the Old Fortress of Corfu (entry €6) overlooking the Ionian Sea. The views are spectacular and the fortress is easy to explore independently.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure — pastry and coffee at a Nafplio bakery
meals.lunch: Snack on the ferry or bus — bring food from a supermarket to save money
meals.dinner: Dinner in Corfu Old Town — try sofrito (veal in white wine sauce) or pastitsada (pasta with rooster), traditional Corfiot dishes, at a local restaurant for €9–12

day_by_day.notes: This is a longer travel day — plan to leave Nafplio early. The bus/ferry combination requires some planning; check KTEL and ferry schedules in advance. Corfu Town is very walkable once you arrive.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus (€1.50–2) to Paleokastritsa on the northwest coast of Corfu — one of the most beautiful spots in Greece. Swim in the stunning turquoise coves, snorkel around the rocks, and explore the small sea caves by renting a paddleboat or kayak (€5–8/hour).
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike up to the Paleokastritsa Monastery (free entry, modest dress required) for breathtaking views over the bays. Then take the bus back toward Corfu Town, stopping at Glyfada Beach — a long sandy beach popular with locals — for more swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Corfu Town for the evening. Join the locals for the evening volta along the Liston and Spianada Square — Europe's second-largest square. Enjoy the lively atmosphere completely free.

meals.breakfast: Fresh bread, local olive oil, and feta from a Corfu Town bakery — €2–3
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish or seafood at a simple beach taverna in Paleokastritsa — €8–10. Sit at the water's edge.
meals.dinner: Mezze dinner in Corfu Town — a spread of local dips, grilled vegetables, and Corfiot cheese with local Robola wine for €9–11

day_by_day.notes: Paleokastritsa is best visited on weekdays to avoid weekend crowds. The local bus system in Corfu is cheap and reliable — pick up a schedule from the bus station in Corfu Town. Bring snorkeling gear if you have it — the water clarity is exceptional.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the north of Corfu by local bus — visit the charming village of Kassiopi with its small harbor, Byzantine castle ruins (free), and clear water beaches. The village has a lovely authentic feel away from the tourist crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Canal d'Amour near Sidari on the way back — a series of sandstone rock formations and narrow sea channels perfect for swimming. Local legend says swimming through the canal guarantees you'll find your true love. Free to access.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Corfu Town. Visit the Archaeological Museum of Corfu (€6) in the early evening if open, or explore the Campiello district — the oldest part of the old town with medieval architecture and hidden squares.

meals.breakfast: Tiganites (Greek pancakes with honey) at a local café in Corfu Town — €3
meals.lunch: Fresh calamari and a Greek salad at a taverna in Kassiopi harbor — €8–10
meals.dinner: Budget dinner at a local souvlaki shop in Corfu Town — souvlaki plate with fries and salad for €7–9

day_by_day.notes: The north of Corfu is less developed and more authentic than the south. Bus connections to Kassiopi and Sidari run several times daily from Corfu Town's New Fortress bus station. Bring cash as some smaller establishments don't accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take the ferry from Corfu back to Igoumenitsa on the mainland, then a KTEL bus south toward Preveza or Lefkada. Cross the causeway bridge (free) onto the island of Lefkada — the only Greek island accessible by road. Check into a budget guesthouse in Lefkada Town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Lefkada Town — a charming town with distinctive earthquake-resistant architecture (upper floors clad in colorful corrugated metal). Walk along the lagoon waterfront and visit the small Venetian fortress of Santa Maura (free to explore externally).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the sunset from the lagoon waterfront in Lefkada Town. The shallow lagoon with its windmills and flamingos (in season) creates a magical atmosphere. Have a drink at a waterfront café.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before ferry departure
meals.lunch: Snack on the ferry or bus — supermarket supplies
meals.dinner: Fresh fish dinner at a waterfront taverna in Lefkada Town — the island is known for excellent local olive oil and fresh seafood. Budget €10–12.

day_by_day.notes: Lefkada is famous for having some of the best beaches in Europe (Porto Katsiki, Egremni). The island is very budget-friendly compared to more touristy Greek islands. Local buses connect the town to the beaches.

day_by_day.morning: Take the local KTEL bus (€3–4 each way) to Porto Katsiki beach on the southwest coast — consistently rated one of the most beautiful beaches in Europe. Dramatic white cliffs drop to turquoise water. Arrive early to claim a spot before the day-trippers arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to nearby Egremni Beach (accessible by steps — about 350 of them!) for a more secluded swimming experience. The water is an extraordinary shade of blue-green. Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing on this stunning stretch of coast.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lefkada Town by bus. Explore the local market street and pick up local products — Lefkada is famous for its salami, olive oil, and honey. Enjoy a relaxed evening in town.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with local Lefkada honey at a café in town — €3
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from the local supermarket to eat at Porto Katsiki — save money and enjoy the beach setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local taverna in Lefkada Town — try the local specialty of meat or fish cooked in local olive oil with herbs for €9–11

day_by_day.notes: Porto Katsiki and Egremni are exposed beaches with no shade — bring a beach umbrella or arrive early. The steps to Egremni were damaged by an earthquake but have been partially restored — check current access. Bring plenty of water.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the east coast of Lefkada by local bus — visit the picturesque village of Nydri with its waterfront cafés and views of the small offshore islands. Take a short boat trip (€5–8) to the nearby islet of Madouri or Skorpios (Onassis's former private island — now accessible by boat tours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Agios Nikitas — a charming traditional village on the northwest coast with a small beach and excellent local tavernas. Walk the coastal path to the quieter Mylos Beach nearby. Swim and relax in the afternoon sun.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening on Lefkada — enjoy a sunset drink at a clifftop café near Agios Nikitas or return to Lefkada Town for a farewell dinner. Reflect on the trip and pack for tomorrow's journey.

meals.breakfast: Freshly baked bread with local cheese and olives from a bakery — €2–3
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish at a taverna in Agios Nikitas — the village is known for excellent seafood. Budget €9–11.
meals.dinner: Celebratory final island dinner — a full mezze spread with local wine, grilled octopus, and fresh bread at a Lefkada Town taverna for €12–14

day_by_day.notes: Agios Nikitas is one of the most authentic and unspoiled villages on Lefkada — worth the bus journey. The local bus schedule can be infrequent in the afternoon, so check return times carefully. Stock up on local products (olive oil, honey) as gifts.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning: Take a leisurely walk around Lefkada Town one last time. Visit the small local market for last-minute food souvenirs. Enjoy a final Greek coffee sitting by the lagoon and watch the morning come alive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel back toward Athens or your departure airport. Take the KTEL bus from Lefkada to Athens (approximately 5–6 hours, €25–30) or to the nearest airport (Preveza/Aktion Airport is the closest, about 20 km away, with connections to Athens). Depending on your return flight schedule, head to Athens International Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Greece with wonderful memories of beaches, ancient history, and incredible local food. If your flight is late, enjoy a final souvlaki at the airport or nearby.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast — a proper sit-down meal of eggs, local cheese, olives, tomatoes, and Greek coffee at a Lefkada café — €4–5
meals.lunch: Packed lunch for the bus journey — supermarket supplies or a gyros wrap to go
meals.dinner: Airport meal or final souvlaki near Athens airport — budget €6–8

day_by_day.notes: Check your return flight details carefully and allow plenty of time for the bus journey back to Athens. The Preveza/Aktion Airport (PVK) may offer a more convenient departure point if flying directly from western Greece. Keep some euros for airport expenses and transport.

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Sunrise Swim at Elafonissi Beach
experiences.description: Visit the famous pink-sand Elafonissi Beach in Crete at sunrise to enjoy the shallow turquoise lagoons and stunning colors before the midday heat sets in. The unique pink hue comes from crushed shells and coral. Spend the morning snorkeling and wading through the shallow waters. Retreat to a nearby taverna for shade and refreshments by late morning.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 to central Athens (~40 min, €9). Check in to your mid-range hotel in the Monastiraki or Koukaki neighborhood. Freshen up and take a gentle stroll around Monastiraki Square to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the atmospheric Monastiraki Flea Market (open late) and enjoy your first views of the illuminated Acropolis. Head to the Psiri neighborhood for a relaxed first dinner.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: Grab a quick gyros wrap from a street kiosk near the airport or Monastiraki Square (€3–5) upon arrival
meals.dinner: Taverna Του Ψαρά (Psiri area) — try grilled octopus, tzatziki, and a carafe of house wine. Budget ~€20–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light. Jet lag and travel fatigue are real — prioritize settling in. Keep luggage light for the metro ride. Book accommodation in Monastiraki, Koukaki, or Syntagma for easy access to sights.

day_by_day.morning: Early visit to the Acropolis (open from 8:00 AM) before the crowds and heat build up. Explore the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and Propylaea. Combined ticket (~€20) includes the Acropolis Museum — save that for the afternoon. Stunning views over Athens in the morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the world-class Acropolis Museum (open until 8 PM on weekdays). Afterward, explore the charming Plaka neighborhood — cobblestone lanes, neoclassical houses, and artisan shops. Stop at Hadrian's Arch and the Temple of Olympian Zeus (included in combined ticket).
day_by_day.evening: Climb Filopappou Hill at sunset for panoramic views of the Acropolis glowing golden. Dinner in Koukaki, one of Athens' most authentic residential neighborhoods.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a neighborhood bakery — try a tiropita (cheese pie) and Greek coffee (~€4–6)
meals.lunch: Light mezze lunch in Plaka — dolmades, hummus, and pita at a shaded taverna (~€12–15)
meals.dinner: Mani Mani Restaurant (Koukaki) — modern Greek cuisine with Mani regional specialties. Try the slow-cooked lamb. ~€25–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes — the Acropolis involves uneven marble surfaces. Bring water and sunscreen. The combined Acropolis ticket is valid for 5 days and covers 7 archaeological sites.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Athens Central Market (Varvakios Agora) — a sensory feast of fresh fish, meat, spices, and olives. Chat with vendors and pick up local snacks. Then visit the National Archaeological Museum (one of the world's greatest), housing the Antikythera Mechanism and Mycenaean gold artifacts. (~€12 entry)
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the upscale Kolonaki neighborhood and climb Lycabettus Hill (funicular or 30-min hike) for the best 360° panoramic views of Athens and the Saronic Gulf. Browse the boutiques and galleries of Kolonaki on the way back.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the sunset from Lycabettus or head to the Thissio neighborhood for rooftop bar drinks with Acropolis views. Dinner in Thissio.

meals.breakfast: At the Central Market area — fresh juice, loukoumades (honey doughnuts) from a street stall (~€3–5)
meals.lunch: Souvlaki lunch near Omonia Square — pork skewers, pita, and chips (~€8–10)
meals.dinner: Stavlos (Thissio) — a converted royal stables turned restaurant/bar. Greek dishes in a beautiful courtyard. ~€20–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The National Archaeological Museum is closed on Mondays. The Varvakios Market is most lively in the morning — arrive before 11 AM. Lycabettus funicular runs every 30 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Cape Sounion (1.5 hrs by KTEL bus from Pedion Areos, ~€7 each way). Visit the magnificent Temple of Poseidon perched on a cliff 60m above the Aegean Sea — one of Greece's most dramatic ancient sites. Lord Byron carved his name into a column here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim at the small beach below the cape or at nearby Legrena Beach. The water is crystal clear and calm in June. Pack a picnic or eat at the small taverna near the site.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Athens by early evening. Explore the vibrant Exarchia neighborhood — bohemian, artsy, and full of authentic local life. Browse independent bookshops and record stores.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or neighborhood café — Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach at Sounion — pick up supplies (olives, cheese, bread, fruit) from a local mini-market in Athens before departure (~€8–10)
meals.dinner: Exarchia taverna — try the daily specials (mageirefta) like moussaka or stifado. Authentic and affordable. ~€15–18 per person.

day_by_day.notes: KTEL buses to Sounion depart from Pedion Areos Park (near Pedion Areos metro). Check the return schedule carefully — last bus back is typically around 7–8 PM. Bring a hat and water as the cape is exposed.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Athens to Heraklion, Crete (1-hour flight, ~€40–70 with Aegean or Sky Express — book in advance). Alternatively, take the overnight ferry (saves a night's accommodation). Arrive in Heraklion and check in to a mid-range hotel or guesthouse. Visit the impressive Palace of Knossos (~€15), the center of Minoan civilization, just 5km from the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Heraklion's old Venetian harbor, the iconic Koules Fortress (€4), and the lively 1866 Street Market — a long open-air bazaar selling local herbs, honey, cheeses, and raki. Visit the Heraklion Archaeological Museum (€10) to see Minoan frescoes and artifacts from Knossos.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Venetian harbor at sunset. Dinner at one of the seafood restaurants overlooking the water.

meals.breakfast: Quick bite at Athens airport or on the plane
meals.lunch: Heraklion market street food — dakos (Cretan rusk salad), local cheese, and olives (~€8–10)
meals.dinner: Peskesi Restaurant (Heraklion) — farm-to-table Cretan cuisine using heirloom recipes. Try the lamb with stamnagathi greens. ~€22–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book your Athens–Heraklion flight well in advance for best prices. If taking the ferry, depart Athens (Piraeus) the night before and arrive in Heraklion in the morning. Knossos is best visited in the morning before tour groups arrive.

day_by_day.morning: FEATURED EXPERIENCE — Sunrise Swim at Elafonissi Beach: Wake up at 4:30 AM for the 2.5-hour drive (or organized tour) to Elafonissi Beach on Crete's southwest coast. Arrive at sunrise (~5:45 AM in June) to experience the famous pink-sand beach and shallow turquoise lagoon in near-total solitude. The pink hue comes from crushed shells of tiny organisms. Wade through the warm, knee-deep lagoon to the small island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the morning and early afternoon at Elafonissi — swim, snorkel, and relax on the pink sand. The beach gets busy by 10 AM, so you'll have had the best hours already. Begin the drive back, stopping at the charming village of Paleochora for lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Heraklion or base yourself in Chania (1 hour from Elafonissi) for the next few days. If staying in Chania, check in and explore the beautiful Venetian old town in the evening.

meals.breakfast: Pack snacks and coffee in a thermos for the pre-dawn drive — pick up supplies the night before
meals.lunch: Fresh fish lunch in Paleochora village on the return journey — grilled sea bream with local salad (~€15–18)
meals.dinner: Chania old town — dinner at a harbor-side restaurant. Try Cretan specialties: boureki (zucchini and cheese pie), snails, and local wine. ~€20–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: This is the highlight beach day — set multiple alarms! Renting a car in Crete is highly recommended (€25–40/day) for flexibility. Elafonissi is a protected nature reserve — no camping, no removing sand or shells. Bring cash as facilities are limited.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Chania's stunning Venetian old town — one of the most beautiful in Greece. Visit the covered market (Agora), the Venetian lighthouse, the Maritime Museum of Crete (€3), and the narrow lanes of the Jewish Quarter (Evraiki). Browse local shops for Cretan olive oil, herbs, and leather goods.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a rooftop bar overlooking the Venetian harbor — the view is spectacular. Dinner in the old town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive 30 minutes east to Balos Lagoon viewpoint (or take a boat trip from Kissamos port, ~€20 return). Balos is another iconic Cretan beach with turquoise waters and white sand — less pink than Elafonissi but equally stunning. Swim and relax.

meals.breakfast: Chania Agora market — fresh pastries, local honey, and Greek coffee (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snacks at Balos — bring water and food as facilities are minimal
meals.dinner: To Maridaki (Chania) — a beloved local fish taverna. Try the fried smelt, grilled octopus, and house raki. ~€18–22 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The road to Balos viewpoint is unpaved and rough — a 4WD or high-clearance vehicle is recommended, or take the boat from Kissamos. Chania's old town is best explored on foot. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the famous Samaria Gorge — one of Europe's longest gorges (16km, 5–7 hours). Start from Xyloskalo (1,250m altitude) and descend through dramatic scenery to the coastal village of Agia Roumeli. The gorge is open May–October. Entry fee €5.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Agia Roumeli beach — a well-earned swim in the Libyan Sea after the hike. The village has a few tavernas for lunch and cold drinks. Take the ferry from Agia Roumeli to Hora Sfakion (€15, ~1 hour), then bus back to Chania.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and recovery evening in Chania. Light dinner and early night.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at 6:00 AM before the hike — hotel or a café near the bus station. Pack energy snacks and 2L of water per person.
meals.lunch: Taverna in Agia Roumeli after completing the gorge — grilled chicken, Greek salad, and cold beer (~€12–15). You've earned it.
meals.dinner: Light mezze dinner in Chania — hummus, taramasalata, grilled vegetables, and bread. ~€12–15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Samaria Gorge is strenuous — wear proper hiking shoes (not sandals), bring plenty of water, sunscreen, and snacks. Buses depart Chania for Xyloskalo at 6:15 AM and 7:30 AM. Book the return ferry in advance in peak season. Not suitable for those with knee problems.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning after the gorge hike. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and explore Chania's backstreets at a relaxed pace. Visit the Etz Hayyim Synagogue (one of the oldest in Europe, free entry) and browse the leather workshops on Skridlof Street.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or take a bus east along the northern coast to the beautiful beach of Falasarna (45 min from Chania) — a wide, sandy beach with clear water and a relaxed vibe. Swim and sunbathe. Alternatively, visit the closer Stavros Beach (made famous by the film Zorba the Greek).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Chania for a cooking class or food tour (book in advance, ~€45–60 per person) — learn to make dakos, spanakopita, and Cretan pasta. Dinner is included in the class.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast or a café in Chania old town — eggs, local cheese, tomatoes, and coffee (~€8–10)
meals.lunch: Beach taverna at Falasarna — fresh fish of the day, Greek salad, and local wine (~€18–22)
meals.dinner: Included in cooking class, or a simple souvlaki wrap if skipping the class (~€5–8)

day_by_day.notes: Falasarna is one of Crete's best beaches — arrive by early afternoon to secure a good spot. The cooking class is a highlight for food lovers — book through Chania Food Tours or similar operators. This is a recovery day after the gorge.

day_by_day.morning: Fly or ferry from Crete to Santorini (Thira). Aegean Airlines flies Heraklion–Santorini in 40 minutes (~€50–80). Alternatively, take the high-speed ferry from Heraklion (2 hours, ~€40). Check in to a mid-range hotel in Fira or Firostefani — avoid Oia for budget reasons but it's worth a day visit. Explore Fira's clifftop paths and the Museum of Prehistoric Thera (€6).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the cable car (€6) or hike down to the old port (Skala). Rent an ATV or quad bike (~€25/day) to explore the island. Drive to the black sand beach of Perissa or Perivolos on the south coast — volcanic sand, clear water, and beach bars.
day_by_day.evening: Drive or take a bus to Oia village for the world-famous Santorini sunset. Arrive by 6 PM to secure a good viewing spot. The caldera views are breathtaking. Dinner in Oia or back in Fira.

meals.breakfast: Airport or ferry snack
meals.lunch: Beach taverna at Perissa — fresh calamari, Greek salad, and cold Mythos beer (~€15–18)
meals.dinner: Fira clifftop restaurant — try fava (yellow split pea purée, a Santorini specialty), tomatokeftedes (tomato fritters), and local Assyrtiko white wine. ~€25–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Santorini is more expensive than Crete — budget accordingly. Book accommodation well in advance for June. The Oia sunset is crowded — arrive early and find a spot on the castle ruins or a quieter path. Assyrtiko wine is Santorini's signature grape — don't miss it.

day_by_day.morning: Take a boat tour of the Santorini caldera (book through your hotel or at the old port, ~€25–35). Visit the active volcanic island of Nea Kameni — hike to the crater and swim in the warm sulfuric hot springs at Palea Kameni. The boat also stops at the picturesque village of Thirassia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Santorini and visit the ancient site of Akrotiri — a remarkably preserved Minoan Bronze Age city buried by the volcanic eruption of 1627 BC (€12 entry). Often called the 'Greek Pompeii.' Afterward, relax at the nearby Red Beach — dramatic red volcanic cliffs and dark sand.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the village of Pyrgos — Santorini's highest point and less touristy than Oia. Climb to the Venetian castle ruins for panoramic island views. Dinner in Pyrgos or Fira.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a bakery in Fira — spanakopita and Greek coffee (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the boat or a snack at the Thirassia village café (~€8–10)
meals.dinner: Metaxy Mas (Exo Gonia village, near Pyrgos) — a beloved local taverna with authentic Santorinian food. Try the slow-cooked lamb and local wine. ~€20–25 per person. Reserve ahead.

day_by_day.notes: The caldera boat tour is a must-do in Santorini. Book the morning departure for the best light. Akrotiri requires advance booking in peak season. Red Beach has limited shade — bring an umbrella. Metaxy Mas is popular with locals and tourists alike — reservations essential.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a kayak or join a sea kayaking tour around the caldera cliffs (~€45–60 for a guided half-day tour). Paddle through sea caves and get unique perspectives of the caldera walls. Alternatively, take a morning wine tour — Santorini has excellent wineries (Santo Wines, Domaine Sigalas) with caldera views and Assyrtiko tastings (~€15–25).
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Kamari Beach on the east coast — a long black sand beach with a lively promenade, water sports, and beach bars. Swim and relax. The water is warm and clear in June.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Santorini — splurge slightly on a special dinner with caldera views. Watch the stars from your hotel terrace or a clifftop bar. Pack for tomorrow's departure.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at a Fira café — eggs, local tomatoes, cheese, and fresh juice (~€8–10)
meals.lunch: Beach taverna at Kamari — grilled fish, tzatziki, and a cold Santorini beer (~€18–22)
meals.dinner: Slightly elevated dinner at a Fira or Firostefani restaurant with caldera views — fresh seafood pasta, local wine, and dessert. ~€30–35 per person as a treat.

day_by_day.notes: This is your last full day in Greece — make it count. The wine tour is excellent for food lovers and pairs well with the trip's culinary theme. Kamari Beach has free public access with paid sunbed rental (~€8–10 for two). Book a taxi or bus to the airport/port for tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Santorini. Wake up for one last sunrise over the caldera — walk the clifftop path from Fira to Firostefani (20 minutes) for a quiet, beautiful farewell view. Return for a leisurely breakfast and final packing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time, take the ferry or flight back to Athens for your connecting Air Serbia flight home. If time allows, spend a few hours in Athens airport's duty-free shops picking up Greek products — olive oil, honey, herbs, and wine make excellent souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Athens International Airport. Reflect on 13 incredible days of beaches, ancient history, and unforgettable Greek food.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast — yogurt with Santorinian honey, fresh fruit, and strong Greek coffee. Savor it.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Santorini port or airport before departure — a last gyros or cheese pie (~€5–8)
meals.dinner: Airport dining in Athens or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours between your Santorini ferry/flight arrival in Athens and your international departure. The Santorini–Athens ferry takes 4–8 hours (depending on type); the flight is 45 minutes. High-speed ferries (SeaJets, Hellenic Seaways) are faster but pricier (~€60–80). Book all transport in advance for June travel.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Sunrise Swim at Elafonissi Beach
experiences.description: Visit the famous pink-sand Elafonissi Beach in Crete at sunrise to enjoy the shallow turquoise lagoons and stunning colors before the midday heat sets in. The unique pink hue comes from crushed shells and coral. Spend the morning snorkeling and wading through the shallow waters. Retreat to a nearby taverna for shade and refreshments by late morning.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) in the cooler morning hours. Sample local cheeses, olives, cured meats, fresh seafood, and traditional Greek pastries like spanakopita and bougatsa. Chat with local vendors and learn about Greek culinary traditions. This indoor-friendly market is a perfect alternative on hot or rainy days, offering an authentic taste of everyday Greek life.

experiences.name: Evening Meze Dinner in Thessaloniki's Ladadika District
experiences.description: As the sun sets and temperatures cool, head to the vibrant Ladadika neighborhood for a traditional Greek meze dinner. Order a spread of grilled octopus, saganaki (fried cheese), tzatziki, dolmades, and fresh bread paired with local ouzo or tsipouro. Thessaloniki is considered Greece's food capital, and this lively district offers dozens of authentic tavernas with outdoor seating perfect for a breezy evening meal.

experiences.name: Sunset Catamaran Cruise around Santorini Caldera
experiences.description: Board a small-group catamaran in the late afternoon to sail around the volcanic Santorini caldera. Swim in the warm Aegean Sea at volcanic hot springs, snorkel over lava formations, and watch the world-famous Santorini sunset from the water. A light Greek dinner with wine is typically included on board. The evening timing avoids the intense midday heat while offering the most spectacular lighting for photos.

experiences.name: Indoor Greek Cooking Class in Heraklion
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class held in a traditional Cretan kitchen, ideal for avoiding midday heat or rainy weather. Learn to prepare authentic Cretan dishes such as dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and loukoumades (honey doughnuts). The instructor sources ingredients from local markets and explains the history and health benefits of the Mediterranean diet. You'll enjoy eating everything you cook as a full meal at the end.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport Eleftherios Venizelos at 14:50 on Air Serbia. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer via private luxury car service to your 5-star hotel in central Athens (recommended: Hotel Grande Bretagne or similar). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around Syntagma Square to begin soaking in the Athenian atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a welcome dinner at a rooftop restaurant in Athens with views of the Acropolis. Recommended: GB Roof Garden Restaurant at Hotel Grande Bretagne or Sense Restaurant at Hotel Athens Tiare — both offer refined Greek cuisine with panoramic city views. Sip on a glass of Assyrtiko white wine and indulge in grilled octopus, fresh seafood, and classic Greek mezedes to kick off the trip.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Light meal at Athens airport arrivals lounge or a quick bite near the hotel upon check-in
meals.dinner: GB Roof Garden Restaurant (Hotel Grande Bretagne) — upscale Greek cuisine with Acropolis views; expect €80–120 per person

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer for a seamless arrival. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel. Athens weather in June averages 23°C — pleasant for an evening walk.

day_by_day.morning: Athens Central Market Food Tour — Head to the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) in the cool morning hours. Explore stalls brimming with fresh fish, cured meats, spices, olives, and local cheeses. Sample traditional Greek street food including koulouri (sesame bread rings), loukoumades (honey doughnuts), and freshly sliced charcuterie. A knowledgeable local guide will narrate the history and culture behind each ingredient.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Acropolis and Parthenon with a private guided tour, avoiding the peak midday heat by timing entry around 12:00–13:00. Afterward, explore the Acropolis Museum at the base of the hill — one of Europe's finest archaeological museums with air-conditioned galleries. Enjoy a leisurely coffee break at the museum's stylish café overlooking the excavation site.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Varoulko Seaside, a Michelin-starred restaurant in Mikrolimano harbor, Piraeus — renowned for its creative seafood tasting menus. Alternatively, dine at Spondi (two Michelin stars) in Pangrati for a French-Mediterranean fusion experience in a romantic garden setting.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast buffet or a traditional Greek breakfast at a nearby café — Greek yogurt with thyme honey, fresh fruit, and spanakopita
meals.lunch: Light mezedes lunch at a taverna near the Acropolis Museum — try taramasalata, tzatziki, grilled halloumi, and fresh pita
meals.dinner: Varoulko Seaside (Michelin-starred) — seafood tasting menu with wine pairing; €120–180 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the Athens Central Market Food Tour in advance with a reputable operator (e.g., Athens Insiders or Culinary Backstreets). Pre-book Acropolis tickets online to skip queues. Dress modestly for the Acropolis site.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Athens and fly to Thessaloniki (approximately 55-minute flight; book with Aegean Airlines). Check into a luxury hotel in Thessaloniki (recommended: Makedonia Palace or Electra Palace Thessaloniki). After settling in, take a morning walk along the scenic Thessaloniki waterfront promenade, admiring the iconic White Tower. Visit the Byzantine Museum for a curated look at the city's rich history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the vibrant Modiano and Kapani covered markets — Thessaloniki's answer to Athens' Varvakios. Browse stalls of local cheeses (especially Thessaloniki's famous bougatsa cream pastry), fresh produce, and spices. Visit the Rotunda and the Arch of Galerius, two remarkable Roman monuments in the city center. Enjoy a mid-afternoon coffee at a stylish café on Aristotelous Square.
day_by_day.evening: Evening Meze Dinner in Thessaloniki's Ladadika District — As the sun sets, head to the vibrant Ladadika neighborhood, the city's historic warehouse district turned dining and entertainment hub. Settle into a traditional taverna for an authentic meze spread: grilled sardines, smoked eggplant dip, cheese saganaki flambéed tableside, and slow-cooked lamb. Pair with local Xinomavro red wine from Naoussa.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or airport lounge in Athens before the flight
meals.lunch: Bougatsa (cream-filled pastry) and local street food at Modiano Market — a quintessential Thessaloniki experience
meals.dinner: Ladadika District taverna (e.g., Tiffany's or Aristotelous Square area restaurants) — traditional meze dinner; €60–90 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the Thessaloniki flight well in advance. Ladadika comes alive after 20:00 — embrace the late Greek dining culture. June evenings in Thessaloniki are warm and perfect for outdoor dining.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Mount Olympus and the village of Litochoro — hire a private driver for the 90-minute journey south. Take a scenic morning hike through the lower trails of Greece's highest mountain (no technical climbing required for lower paths). Breathe in the pine-scented air and enjoy views of the Enipeas gorge. Visit the charming village of Litochoro for a coffee break.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Thessaloniki and visit the stunning Ano Poli (Upper Town) — the old Byzantine quarter with preserved Ottoman-era architecture, cobblestone lanes, and panoramic views over the city and the Thermaic Gulf. Explore the Heptapyrgion fortress and wander through the atmospheric neighborhood at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar in Thessaloniki (recommended: Roof Garden at Electra Palace or Hyatt Regency rooftop). Follow with dinner at a refined modern Greek restaurant — try Extravaganza or Clochard for creative interpretations of northern Greek cuisine, featuring dishes like rabbit stifado, truffle-laced pasta, and local game meats.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fresh pastries, Greek yogurt, local honey, and cold cuts
meals.lunch: Traditional taverna lunch in Litochoro village — grilled meats, village salad, and local mountain herbs
meals.dinner: Clochard Restaurant, Thessaloniki — upscale modern Greek; €70–100 per person with wine

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for both Olympus trails and Ano Poli's cobblestones. Private driver for the Olympus day trip can be arranged through the hotel concierge. Carry water and sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Thessaloniki to Heraklion, Crete (approximately 1 hour 20 minutes with Aegean Airlines). Check into a luxury resort near Heraklion (recommended: Domes Noruz Chania or Knossos Royal Beach Resort). After check-in, visit the Palace of Knossos — the legendary Minoan palace complex, one of Europe's oldest and most fascinating archaeological sites. Hire a private guide for an in-depth tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indoor Greek Cooking Class in Heraklion — Join a hands-on cooking class held in a traditional Cretan kitchen. Learn to prepare iconic Cretan dishes: dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi (wild greens), and loukoumades with Cretan honey. The class is held indoors, making it a perfect midday activity during the warmest hours. Enjoy your creations as lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Heraklion's charming old harbor area and the impressive Koules Venetian Fortress at sunset. Dine at a premium seafood restaurant along the harbor — recommended: Peskesi (farm-to-table Cretan cuisine in a beautifully restored mansion) or Ippokambos for fresh catch of the day with Cretan wine.

meals.breakfast: Airport lounge or hotel breakfast upon arrival
meals.lunch: Dishes prepared during the cooking class — an immersive and delicious midday meal
meals.dinner: Peskesi Restaurant, Heraklion — authentic Cretan farm-to-table; €65–95 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class in advance (Crete Cooking Lessons or similar operators). Knossos is best visited in the morning before crowds peak. Keep afternoons free for indoor activities during the warmest part of the day.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning drive west along Crete's northern coast to Elafonissi Beach (approximately 2.5 hours from Heraklion — arrange a private luxury transfer). Arrive at the famous pink-sand Elafonissi Beach at sunrise to enjoy the shallow turquoise lagoon in near-total solitude before the crowds arrive. Wade through the warm, knee-deep waters of the lagoon, marvel at the rose-tinted sand caused by crushed coral, and swim in the crystal-clear Libyan Sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the late morning and early afternoon relaxing on Elafonissi Beach with a private beach setup (umbrella, sunbeds, chilled drinks). Explore the small island accessible by wading across the lagoon. Begin the return journey to Heraklion around 14:00, stopping at a traditional village taverna in the Kissamos region for a late lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Heraklion resort for a relaxing evening. Enjoy a spa treatment at the hotel (massage or thalassotherapy). Dine at the resort's signature restaurant or venture out to a local wine bar for a curated Cretan wine tasting paired with local cheeses and charcuterie.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast or light snacks prepared by the hotel before departure (request the night before)
meals.lunch: Traditional Cretan taverna in Kissamos or Platanos village — fresh grilled fish, horta (wild greens), and local olive oil
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant or Heraklion wine bar — Cretan wine tasting with mezedes; €50–80 per person

day_by_day.notes: Depart by 05:30–06:00 to reach Elafonissi at sunrise. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and water shoes for the lagoon. The beach gets very crowded by 10:00 in summer — early arrival is essential for the premium experience.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the charming Venetian town of Chania (approximately 1 hour west of Heraklion by private transfer). Wander through the narrow alleyways of the old town, visit the covered market (Agora), and admire the picturesque Venetian harbor with its iconic lighthouse. Browse artisan shops selling Cretan olive oil, herbs, and handmade leather goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Botanical Park and Gardens of Crete near Fournes village — a lush, beautifully landscaped park with exotic plants, fruit trees, and mountain streams. Enjoy a peaceful walk through the gardens and a light lunch at the park's organic restaurant. Return to Chania for a leisurely afternoon swim at Nea Chora beach or the nearby Agia Marina beach.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner at a premium restaurant in Chania's Venetian harbor — recommended: Tamam (in a converted Ottoman bathhouse) or Elia & Diosmos for creative Cretan-Mediterranean cuisine. Enjoy fresh lobster pasta, grilled sea bream, and local Vidiano white wine as boats bob gently in the harbor.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Heraklion before departure
meals.lunch: Organic lunch at the Botanical Park restaurant — fresh salads, local cheeses, and seasonal Cretan produce
meals.dinner: Elia & Diosmos, Chania — upscale Cretan cuisine; €70–100 per person; return to Heraklion by private transfer after dinner

day_by_day.notes: Chania is one of Crete's most beautiful towns — allow plenty of time to wander without a rigid schedule. Book dinner reservations in advance, especially for harbor-view tables.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Heraklion to Santorini (approximately 45 minutes with Aegean Airlines or Sky Express). Check into a luxury cave hotel in Oia or Imerovigli (recommended: Canaves Oia Epitome, Mystique, or Andronis Luxury Suites). These iconic cliffside properties offer private plunge pools and breathtaking caldera views. Spend the morning settling in and enjoying the hotel's infinity pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the iconic village of Oia on foot — wander through the blue-domed churches, whitewashed alleyways, and art galleries. Visit the Oia Castle ruins for panoramic caldera views. Browse high-end boutiques selling local jewelry, ceramics, and art. Stop for a refreshing Santorini Assyrtiko wine tasting at a cliffside wine bar (recommended: Venetsanos Winery or Santo Wines).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Catamaran Cruise around the Santorini Caldera — Board a small-group luxury catamaran in the late afternoon to sail around the volcanic caldera. Swim in the hot springs near the volcanic island of Nea Kameni, snorkel in crystal-clear waters, and watch the legendary Santorini sunset from the sea. Onboard catering includes fresh seafood, Greek salads, and chilled wine.

meals.breakfast: Airport lounge or light breakfast at Heraklion hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Light mezedes and wine at Santo Wines winery terrace — spectacular caldera views
meals.dinner: Onboard catering during the catamaran cruise, followed by a late dinner at the hotel's restaurant or a cliffside taverna in Oia

day_by_day.notes: Book the catamaran cruise well in advance — small-group luxury options (e.g., Santorini Sailing or Sunset Oia Sailing) fill up quickly in June. Sunset in Santorini in late June is around 20:45 — plan the cruise departure for 17:00–17:30.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Akrotiri — the remarkably preserved Minoan Bronze Age settlement buried by the same volcanic eruption that shaped Santorini's caldera. Often called the 'Pompeii of the Aegean,' the site features multi-story buildings, frescoes, and sophisticated drainage systems. The site is covered, making it comfortable even in warm weather.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the black-sand beaches of Santorini — Perissa and Perivolos beaches on the island's southeastern coast. Rent a premium sunbed setup at a beach club (recommended: Wet Stories or Seaside Beach Bar) and enjoy the dramatic contrast of black volcanic sand against the deep blue Aegean. Take a refreshing swim and enjoy cocktails by the water.
day_by_day.evening: Romantic dinner at one of Santorini's finest cliffside restaurants — recommended: Lycabettus Restaurant in Imerovigli (stunning caldera views, creative Greek cuisine) or Selene in Pyrgos (two-time winner of best Greek restaurant, farm-to-table philosophy). Pair your meal with a bottle of Santorini's celebrated Assyrtiko wine.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast with caldera views — fresh fruit, Greek yogurt, eggs, and pastries
meals.lunch: Beach club lunch at Perivolos — fresh seafood, salads, and cocktails with sea views
meals.dinner: Selene Restaurant, Pyrgos — award-winning Greek cuisine; €100–150 per person with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Akrotiri requires advance ticket booking. Wear comfortable shoes for the archaeological site. Perissa beach is a 20-minute drive from Oia — arrange a private taxi or rent an ATV for island exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at the hotel — enjoy a private plunge pool breakfast with caldera views (arrange with the hotel in advance). Take a morning yoga session if offered by the hotel, or simply relax and soak in the extraordinary scenery. Later, take a scenic hike along the famous Fira-to-Oia caldera trail (approximately 10 km, 3–4 hours) for unparalleled views of the caldera, volcanic islands, and Aegean Sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Fira (Santorini's capital) after the hike. Explore the town's Museum of Prehistoric Thera, which houses stunning Akrotiri frescoes and artifacts. Browse the upscale shops and galleries along the caldera edge. Enjoy a refreshing cold brew coffee or fresh juice at a café before returning to the hotel by cable car or private transfer.
day_by_day.evening: Private wine and food pairing experience at Venetsanos Winery — perched dramatically on the caldera cliff, this historic winery offers curated tastings of Santorini's indigenous varieties (Assyrtiko, Athiri, Aidani) paired with local cheeses, cherry tomatoes, and fava. Watch the sun dip below the horizon from the winery's spectacular terrace.

meals.breakfast: In-room or poolside breakfast at the hotel — a luxurious private experience
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Fira after the hike — fresh salads, grilled vegetables, and local fava bean dip at a caldera-view café
meals.dinner: Venetsanos Winery wine and food pairing experience, followed by dinner at a Fira restaurant — Koukoumavlos for innovative Greek fine dining; €90–130 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Fira-to-Oia hike is best done in the morning before temperatures peak. Wear sunscreen, a hat, and carry 2 liters of water. The trail is well-marked but can be uneven — wear proper footwear. Book the Venetsanos winery experience in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Santorini back to Athens (approximately 45 minutes). Check into a luxury hotel in Athens for the final nights (recommended: Hotel Grande Bretagne, King George Hotel, or Electra Metropolis). After settling in, visit the National Archaeological Museum — one of the world's greatest collections of ancient Greek art, including the Antikythera Mechanism and the Mask of Agamemnon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming Monastiraki and Plaka neighborhoods — Athens' most atmospheric districts. Browse antique shops, artisan boutiques, and souvenir stores in Monastiraki Flea Market. Climb to the Areopagus Hill (Mars Hill) for a free, crowd-free view of the Acropolis and the city. Enjoy a traditional Greek coffee at a café in Plaka's shaded squares.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of Athens' most celebrated restaurants — recommended: Hytra (one Michelin star, innovative Greek cuisine with Acropolis views) or Nolan (creative fusion of Greek and Japanese techniques). Celebrate the penultimate evening of the trip with a premium tasting menu and exceptional Greek wines.

meals.breakfast: Airport lounge in Santorini or light breakfast at the hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Traditional lunch in Plaka — moussaka, pastitsio, and fresh Greek salad at a classic taverna (e.g., Scholarchio or Byzantino)
meals.dinner: Hytra Restaurant, Athens — Michelin-starred innovative Greek cuisine; €120–160 per person with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book the National Archaeological Museum visit for the morning to avoid afternoon crowds. The Monastiraki Flea Market is most vibrant on Sunday mornings — Friday will still offer a good selection. Confirm dinner reservations well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Acropolis and surrounding ancient sites — if not visited in depth on Day 2, this is the perfect opportunity for a comprehensive exploration with a licensed archaeologist guide. Visit the Parthenon, Erechtheion, Temple of Athena Nike, and the Odeon of Herodes Atticus. Descend to the Ancient Agora and the remarkably preserved Temple of Hephaestus.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the upscale Kolonaki neighborhood — Athens' most elegant district, home to designer boutiques, art galleries, and sophisticated cafés. Take the funicular up to Lycabettus Hill for the best panoramic view of Athens, the Acropolis, and the Saronic Gulf on a clear day. Enjoy a coffee or cocktail at the hilltop café. Spend the late afternoon at leisure — shopping, spa, or relaxing at the hotel pool.
day_by_day.evening: Premium farewell dinner experience — book a private dining experience or chef's table at a top Athens restaurant. Alternatively, enjoy a rooftop dinner at the hotel with Acropolis views illuminated at night. Recommended: Tudor Hall at King George Hotel (rooftop, stunning Acropolis views, refined Greek-Mediterranean cuisine) — the perfect way to end the Greek adventure.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast — take your time on this penultimate morning
meals.lunch: Elegant lunch at a Kolonaki restaurant — try Vezene or Aleria for modern Greek cuisine in a sophisticated setting; €50–70 per person
meals.dinner: Tudor Hall, King George Hotel — rooftop fine dining with Acropolis views; €100–140 per person with wine

day_by_day.notes: The Acropolis is best visited early morning (08:00 opening) to beat crowds and heat. Lycabettus Hill funicular runs regularly — check current operating hours. Pack any purchased souvenirs and gifts this evening to prepare for departure.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Athens — enjoy a relaxed hotel breakfast and take a last stroll through the city. Visit the Zappeion Gardens and the Panathenaic Stadium (the original Olympic stadium, built entirely of marble) for a final dose of ancient history. Pick up any last-minute gifts at the airport or in the Monastiraki area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel and transfer to Athens International Airport via private luxury car service. Allow at least 3 hours before departure for international flights. Enjoy a final Greek meal at the airport or in a nearby restaurant before heading to departures.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Athens — carry with you memories of pink-sand beaches, volcanic sunsets, Michelin-starred mezedes, and the timeless beauty of Greece.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — savor every last bite of Greek yogurt, honey, and fresh pastries
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch near the hotel or at the airport — fresh Greek salad, grilled souvlaki, and a final glass of Assyrtiko
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Arrange airport transfer the night before. Keep travel documents, boarding passes, and any duty-free purchases easily accessible.
